subject: Post-call: trial credit checkpoint & cost qualification
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gutierrez <elena@finwise.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (trial credits & cost qualification)

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning, Elena — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: validate FinWise's summary-generation workflow on Redwood with representative load.
- Key success criteria from your side: 95th pct latency < 700ms for short summaries, cost target ~$350-$600/1M tokens as a target operating range, and predictable unit economics for a production pilot.
- Estimated initial volume: you mentioned 5–10M tokens/month for an initial pilot window (scale to 20M+ depending on early results).

What we propose next: 
1) Apply a one-time trial credit (see proposed figure below) to give you a runway while you run integration tests and validate latency/cost.
2) A short tech check-in with our infra team to lock prompt size, batching settings, and a KV-cache plan (30m).
3) Agree on a simple consumption target so we can proactively monitor burn rate and suggest batching/quantization tweaks.

Prelim economics: based on the model variant we demoed (fast-gen-1.5), we estimate unit costs in the ballpark of $480/1M tokens at current allocated profiles. With batching and prefix caching we typically see 20–35% downward movement; we'll monitor and adjust.

Proposed credit: $3,000 (applied to your account, rough parity with ~6–7M tokens on the profile above) + a 14-day trial extension if you need more time for end-to-end validation. This is discretionary on our side and I can route for approval — asking Ben for a quick sign-off.

Attachments: redwood-trial-estimate.xlsx (simple cost model), redwood-trial-terms.pdf (trial addendum).

If that sounds reasonable, can we schedule the tech sync for Thursday 2/16 at 10am PT? Also looping Craig from Procurement if you want terms/PO discussion.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

---

From: Elena Gutierrez <elena@finwise.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Craig M. <craig.m@finwise.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (trial credits & cost qualification)

Appreciate the recap, Lauren — that aligns with our internal notes. Couple of clarifications from my side before the tech sync:

1) Volume: the 5–10M tokens/month is what we expect for the discovery cohort (approx. 2k–4k summaries/day); if early results look good we intend to double in month 2.
2) Cost target: when I quoted $350–$600/1M tokens, I was thinking of a blended rate including embeddings and reranking calls; our finance team will want to see per-unit breakout.
3) Credits: $3,000 sounds helpful; could you confirm if that credit can only be used for generation tokens or both generation + embeddings? Also, any limits on model variants we can use under the credit?

If you can send a short per-call/per-token breakout and the proposed terms I can get Procurement (Craig) to sign off faster. Thursday 2/16 10am PT works for a tech sync.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Gutierrez
VP Product, FinWise AI
elena@finwise.ai

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gutierrez <elena@finwise.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Craig M. <craig.m@finwise.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 13:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (trial credits & cost qualification)

Great questions — answers inline below and attached a quick one-pager.

- Credit scope: the $3,000 trial credit can be applied to both generation and embeddings; we can split by tag if you prefer (we'll show a token-level breakdown in the Console).
- Model constraints: credit applies to any model in the Redwood catalog, with the exception of our experimental large-llm premium variants (we'll list allowed SKUs in the addendum). The fast-gen-1.5 profile used in the demo is included.
- Per-call breakout: see tab "Unit Econ" in redwood-trial-estimate.xlsx — high level: generation ~ $480/1M tokens (fast-gen-1.5), embeddings ~ $950/1M embedding-units (smaller vectors), rerank/other calls are priced per-call but typically negligible vs long-form generation. This is an initial plug number; we will instrument and re-profile after first 1M tokens.

Operational note: for the kinds of latency you're targeting we recommend enabling short-sequence batching and KV prefix caching; those two simple controls usually cut median token-cost by 15–25% while preserving latency. We'll run those settings during the pilot unless you ask us not to.

I've attached the estimate and trial-terms. If Procurement/Craig is good, can I route for credit sign-off from Finance? Ben — can you confirm the approval workflow and whether $3k + 14-day extension is ok?

Thanks — Lauren

[Attachment: redwood-trial-estimate.xlsx]
[Attachment: redwood-trial-terms.pdf]

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: approval request — FinWise trial credit $3k + 14d extension (deal HS-48921)

Ben — quick ask: requesting approval to apply $3,000 in trial credit to FinWise AI (deal HS-48921) and give a 14-day trial extension. Rationale: they have an engaged product team, clear initial volumes (5–10M tokens/mo), and a reasonable cost target. The credit covers roughly ~6–7M token equivalents on the initial profile and should be sufficient to validate latency & unit economics.

Conditions I propose: 
- Credit expires 60 days from issuance unless they convert to paid contract.
- No overlap with other promotional credits.
- If burn goes > $2k in 7 days, we trigger an ops sync + suggestion for throttling/batching.

Supporting docs attached (cost estimate + trial terms). If you can approve quickly I will let Procurement/Craig know and schedule the tech sync for Thursday 2/16 10am PT.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Lauren

Lauren — approved. 

- Approve one-time $3,000 credit to FinWise (deal HS-48921).
- Approve 14-day trial extension.
- Conditions accepted: credit expires 60 days from issuance; trigger ops sync if usage exceeds $2k in first 7 days.

Please apply credit and update HubSpot (deal HS-48921) with the credit line item and the DocuSign link for the trial addendum. Finance will reconcile against promotional credits ledger.

Ben Carter

ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Credit applied + tech sync confirmed (Thu 2/16 10am PT)

Hi Elena / Craig — quick update: 

- Finance approved the one-time $3,000 trial credit and the 14-day extension. Credit has been applied to your FinWise account and should show up in the Console under Billing > Credits.
- I've added the credit line item to HubSpot (deal HS-48921) and attached the DocuSign link for the trial addendum: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123-redwood-finwise-trial. Please sign so Legal has the paper trail.
- Tech sync confirmed for Thu 2/16 at 10am PT — Marissa (cc'd) from our infra team will join to walk batching/cache settings.

Next steps for you: 
1) Sign the DocuSign trial addendum (link above).
2) Share a sample of expected summaries (see pilot-usage-sample.csv) so our infra team can pre-configure prompts and KV prefixes.
3) We will instrument the Console dashboards and set an early alert at $2k burn in 7 days — we will reach out proactively if we see spikes.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync tomorrow.

Best,
Lauren
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
